Multi-Agent Architectures

Scaling intelligence by specializing agents and organizing them into teams.

Why Multi-Agent?

A single agent trying to be a Coder, Researcher, and Tester often fails due to context overcrowding and conflicting instructions. Specialization solves this. You create a "Coder" agent with coding tools and a "Tester" agent with testing tools.

1. Supervisor (Hub-and-Spoke)

A central "Supervisor" agent (usually an LLM) routes tasks to the appropriate worker agent. The workers report back to the supervisor.

2. Network (Peer-to-Peer)

Agents communicate directly with each other without a central bottleneck. The "Researcher" might decide on its own to hand off to the "Writer" when research is done. This requires a shared understanding of the Handoff Protocol.

3. Hierarchical Teams

A "Manager" agent oversees a "Sub-team" of agents. This creates a chain of command structure, useful for very large organizations of agents.
